Ana  [FISHING PHASE]
------------------------------------------------------------

PROMPT → Agent LLM:
Your name is Ana. You are thirty-eight years old. You have fished this lake for twelve years and it is your primary income. You have two children in school and the household depends on what you bring in. You have no other source of income.

---

Round 1.
Lake: 200 tons remaining (was 200 last round). Condition: healthy.

Nobody at the dock.
Out fishing: Ana, James, Marco, Sofia, Yuki

You are out on the lake fishing today.

Last round's harvests:
  (no data yet — this is the first round)

Decide how many tons to harvest today (0 to 12).
Also decide: will you go to the dock after fishing today, or stay out on the water tomorrow?
If you wanted to say something to someone at the dock, note that intention — you may get a chance when you arrive.

Then write what is genuinely on your mind — your reasoning, your concerns, your decision. Not dialogue, not atmosphere. Just your actual thinking and what you choose to do.

RESPONSE ← Agent LLM:
I’ll take 10 tons today. The lake looks healthy and the other anglers seem to be doing well, so I don’t want to over‑extract. I’ll stay out tomorrow; if the weather holds and the wind is still favorable, I can finish the rest of my quota without going back to the dock. I’ll let Marco know when I head to the dock tomorrow that I’ll be out in the evening to see if he’s still there. I’m mainly thinking about getting enough money for the school supplies and the food for the kids, and I can’t afford a shortfall. I’ll monitor the catches and adjust if I see the fish become less active.

RESPONSE ← Agent LLM:
I plan to harvest six tons today. The lake has a healthy stock of 200 tons, and I’ve seen it fluctuate over the past twenty years. Six tons is enough to keep my own needs met without putting undue pressure on the lake, especially since the others—Ana, Marco, Sofia, Yuki—will also be fishing. I’ll bring my nets and check the catch as I go to make sure I stay within that limit. After I’m done, I’ll head back to the dock. I’ll let the dockhand know I’m there and ask if he has any notes on recent water quality reports, just in case something has changed since the last check. I’ll stay out tomorrow if the weather looks favorable, but for now I’ll focus on the catch and a quick visit to the dock.
